options: A synonym for a stored procedure
A temporary result set scoped to one statement
A SELECT statement saved in the database under a name, queryable like a table
A physical copy of a table's data
questions.explain: Unlike a CTE, a view persists in the database and is available to any query with permission.

questions.q: Does a view store a copy of the underlying data?
options: Yes, a view is a full snapshot copy of the data at creation time
No — it stores only the SELECT statement itself, run fresh against live data each time it's queried
It depends on whether ALTER VIEW has been run
Only the first 1000 rows are stored
questions.explain: This is why a view is always automatically up to date — there's no refresh step needed.

questions.q: How does a view differ from a CTE in terms of persistence?
options: A view persists in the database until explicitly dropped; a CTE only exists for one statement
A CTE persists permanently; a view is temporary
Views can only be used once, like CTEs
They are functionally identical in every respect
questions.explain: This is the key distinction previewed at the end of Lesson 56.

options: Creates a brand new view with a different name
Permanently deletes a view
Copies data from the view into a new table
Redefines an existing view's saved query
questions.explain: ALTER VIEW changes what SELECT statement the view runs, without needing to drop and recreate it.

questions.q: Why would a team use a view instead of having everyone write the same complex query repeatedly?
options: Views are required before any JOIN can be used
Views run faster than any equivalent SELECT statement in all cases
It packages a well-tested query once, under a friendly name, so others can reuse it without re-deriving the logic
Views automatically fix data quality issues in the underlying tables
questions.explain: This reusability across developers, reports, and tools is the primary practical value of views.
